answer: Before managing tax-forfeited land any other way, the county must first offer forfeited parcels at a public auction run by the county auditor and sell to the highest bidder.
quote: Prior to managing tax-forfeited lands as otherwise provided in this chapter, a county must first offer tax-forfeited parcels for sale pursuant to this section ... The county auditor must sell the property at a public auction to the highest bidder in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
note: Section added by 2024 c 127 art 70 s 4.

answer: The sale must occur within six months of the filing of the certificate of forfeiture or the date the property is vacated, whichever is later, with notice published at least 30 days before the sale starts.
quote: The sale under this section must occur within six months of either the filing of the certificate of forfeiture pursuant to section 281.23, subdivision 9 , or the date the property is vacated by the occupant, whichever is later. Notice of the sale under this subdivision must be provided by publication in newspapers, websites, and other forums that serve diverse communities in the county where the property is located at least 30 days before the commencement of the sale.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: The law allows the public auction to be held online; a county may also sell tax-forfeited lands through an online auction with posted and website notice at least ten days before it begins.
quote: in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction. ... may sell tax-forfeited lands through an online auction. When an online auction is used to sell tax-forfeited lands, the county auditor shall post a physical notice of the online auction and shall publish a notice of the online auction on its website not less than ten days before the online auction begins
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
note: Chapter 282 sets no bidder-registration rule that was found; see county rows.

source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
note: Chapter 282 sets no auction deposit rule that was found.

answer: The starting price is the estimated market value from the most recent assessment, and the property may not sell below it for 30 days. If no buyer pays it, the price drops to the minimum bid: the delinquent taxes, special assessments, penalties, interest and costs.
quote: "minimum bid" means the sum of delinquent taxes, special assessments, penalties, interests, and costs assigned to the parcel. ... the initial price of the property, which is equal to the estimated market value, as determined by the most recent assessment. The property must not be sold for less than the initial price for 30 days after it is initially made available at auction. If no buyer is willing to pay the initial price, the price for the property must be reduced to the minimum bid.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
note: 282.005 states no payment deadline; set by the county's sale terms.

answer: A $25 fee is collected in addition to the sale price when the land is fully paid for.
quote: and upon full payment for the land, plus a $25 fee in addition to the sale price, the sale shall be complete and a conveyance of the land shall be issued to the purchaser
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: The law provides for repurchase by an interested party before the public sale, by paying all delinquent taxes and assessments with penalties, interest and costs.
quote: Prior to the public sale required under this section, an interested party may repurchase the property by payment of the sum of all delinquent taxes and assessments computed under section 282.251 , together with penalties, interest, and costs, that accrued or would have accrued if the parcel of land had not forfeited.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: After full payment, a conveyance is issued to the purchaser according to the land's status on forfeiture. Any conveyance of forfeited land reserves all minerals and mineral rights to the state.
quote: a conveyance of the land shall be issued to the purchaser as provided by the appropriate statutes according to the status of the land upon forfeiture. ... Any conveyance of forfeited lands shall be subject to exceptions and reservations in this state, in trust for the taxing districts of all minerals and mineral rights.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: Forfeiture extinguishes all liens, claims and encumbrances except: interested parties' rights to surplus proceeds, redemption rights under federal law, easements and rights-of-way of holders who are not interested parties, and recorded real covenants.
quote: The forfeiture of the property extinguishes all liens, claims, and encumbrances other than: (1) the rights of interested parties to surplus proceeds under this section; (2) rights of redemption provided under federal law; (3) easements and rights-of-way holders who are not interested parties; and (4) benefits or burdens of any real covenants filed of record as of the date of forfeiture.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: If no buyer pays the minimum bid, the state is deemed to have bought the property by a credit bid, and the parcel may be disposed of under the rest of chapter 282.
quote: If no buyer is willing to pay the minimum bid, the state is deemed to have purchased the property through a credit bid and the parcels may be disposed of as otherwise provided in this chapter.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
note: No statewide buyer due-diligence statement found in chapter 282; see the Ramsey county row.

answer: After all parcels in a county sale have been offered to the highest bidder, the county auditor sells any remaining parcels to anyone offering the appraised value.
quote: and shall sell them to the highest bidder, but not for a sum less than the appraised value, until all of the parcels of land have been offered. Then the county auditor shall sell any remaining parcels to anyone offering to pay the appraised value
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: Remaining parcels are sold by the county auditor to anyone offering to pay the appraised value. A person who could have repurchased the parcel may not buy it for less than all taxes, assessments, penalties, interest and costs due at forfeiture.
quote: Then the county auditor shall sell any remaining parcels to anyone offering to pay the appraised value, except that if the person could have repurchased a parcel of property under section 282.012 or 282.241 , that person may not purchase that same parcel of property at the sale under this subdivision for a purchase price less than the sum of all taxes, assessments, penalties, interest, and costs due at the time of forfeiture
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: Parcels are appraised by the county board, and the sale may not be for less than the appraised value, except under the city-sale alternate procedure.
quote: Any parcels of land proposed to be sold shall be first appraised by the county board of the county in which the parcels lie. ... The sale must not be for less than the appraised value except as provided in subdivision 7a.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: A $25 fee is collected in addition to the sale price on full payment.
quote: and upon full payment for the land, plus a $25 fee in addition to the sale price, the sale shall be complete
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
note: Chapter 282 names no buyer form that was found; set by each county.

answer: Cash only, unless the county board has adopted a resolution for sale on terms. On terms, at least ten percent is paid at purchase and the balance in no more than ten equal annual installments.
quote: The parcels must be sold for cash only, unless the county board of the county has adopted a resolution providing for their sale on terms, in which event the resolution controls with respect to the sale. When the sale is made on terms other than for cash only (1) a payment of at least ten percent of the purchase price must be made at the time of purchase, and the balance must be paid in no more than ten equal annual installments
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: After full payment, a conveyance is issued according to the land's status on forfeiture; all minerals and mineral rights are reserved to the state.
quote: a conveyance of the land shall be issued to the purchaser as provided by the appropriate statutes according to the status of the land upon forfeiture. ... Any conveyance of forfeited lands shall be subject to exceptions and reservations in this state, in trust for the taxing districts of all minerals and mineral rights.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: The sale continues until all parcels are sold or until the county board orders a reappraisal or withdraws parcels from sale.
quote: The sale must continue until all the parcels are sold or until the county board orders a reappraisal or withdraws any or all of the parcels from sale.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

answer: Besides the price, 3% of the price goes to the Tax Forfeited Land Assurance Fund, $25 for the State Deed, 0.33% of the price (minimum $1.65) for State Deed Tax, and $46 to record the State Deed.

A recording fee of $46 will be collected to record the State Deed once it is received from the Department of Revenue.
